Bellavia Foods Inc. - Q3 2023 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Bellavia Foods Inc. Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the question-and-answer session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you're using a landline or the raise hand button if you're using the webcast. To withdraw your question, press star then two. We ask that you limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Bellavia Foods' Q3 2023 results. Joining me on the call are John Ramirez, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Financial Officer; Alex Chen, Chief Growth Officer; and David Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to John.

John Ramirez (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on seven key areas: Revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance, Market share trends for major brands, Impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions, Impact of new product innovations and launches, Organic revenue growth: overall and by region, Organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter/year, and Performance of key brands and product categories.

First, regarding Revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance. We delivered another quarter of resilient performance amid a dynamic macroeconomic environment, with net revenues up 6% to $3.2 billion, organic growth of 4.2%, and adjusted EPS of $0.85, beating our guidance midpoint. Today, we are reaffirming our full-year guidance ranges for revenue, organic growth, and adjusted EPS, while narrowing the EPS range to reflect the strength we've seen year-to-date and our heightened confidence in the back half. Specifically, net revenues of $12.6 billion to $12.9 billion, implying 5% to 7% reported growth and 4% to 6% organic growth. This is in line with our prior guide and reflects continued momentum in volume-driven categories, partially offset by targeted price elasticity management in value segments. Adjusted operating profit of $2.45 billion to $2.55 billion, representing 5% to 8% growth on an adjusted basis. Adjusted EPS of $3.25 to $3.35, narrowed from our prior $3.20 to $3.40 range. This assumes an adjusted effective tax rate of 23.5% and roughly 1.2 billion weighted average shares outstanding. Core productivity savings of approximately $450 million, up slightly from our prior outlook, driven by our ongoing Supply Chain Resilience 2.0 initiative, which includes AI-powered demand forecasting and robotic process automation in our 45 North American plants.

Our Nutrition & Snacks segment, which includes powerhouse brands like CrunchMax and NutriTrail protein snacks, remains our growth engine. Q3 organic revenues grew 7%, fueled by 3% volume gains in premium health-oriented SKUs—think our new 30% plant-based reformulation of CrunchMax, which captured 1.2 share points in the U.S. salty snacks category per Nielsen data. For the full year, we expect Nutrition & Snacks to deliver 6% to 8% organic growth, with gross margins expanding 150 basis points to 41%, thanks to cocoa hedging strategies that mitigated the 20% YoY commodity spike we've seen industry-wide, similar to what Hershey and Mondelez have navigated.

Beverages, representing 40% of our portfolio with brands like HydroBoost hydration drinks and PureVita juices, posted 3% organic growth in Q3, with volumes flat but pricing up 4% amid easing inflation. We're reaffirming 3% to 5% full-year organic growth here, bolstered by our Flavor Forward innovation pipeline—launched last month, featuring low-sugar RTD coffees that have already driven 15% trial rates in test markets, echoing the success of PepsiCo's Starbucks partnership. Margins should hold at 35% to 37%, as PET resin costs trend down 10% sequentially per PCI data.

North America, 75% of revenues, expect 5% organic growth for the year, with consumer staples resilience shining through. Premiumization trends are intact—health-focused products like our NutriTrail line grew 12% despite soft discretionary spending. We're on track for 200 basis points of North American gross margin expansion via localized sourcing, reducing trans-Pacific freight exposure by 25%.

EMEA, 15%, reaffirming 4% to 6% organic growth, navigating regulatory headwinds like the UK's HFSS advertising restrictions. Our plant-based dairy alternatives gained 2 points of share in Germany, offsetting a 1% volume dip in core carbonates.

APAC and LatAm, 10%, upside potential here with 8% to 10% growth, driven by e-commerce penetration—now 18% of APAC sales via platforms like Tmall. In Brazil, HydroBoost volumes surged 14% on soccer sponsorship tie-ins, mirroring Ambev's playbook.

This reaffirmed guidance underscores our three-pillar strategy: Portfolio Elevation, Operational Agility, and Sustainable Growth. First, portfolio elevation: We're accelerating divestitures of low-single-digit margin legacy brands, targeting $300 million in proceeds by year-end to fuel bolt-on M&A in high-growth adjacencies like functional beverages. Our R&D spend is up 12% to $250 million, with 20 new SKUs launching Q4, emphasizing clean label formulations amid 65% consumer preference for no-artificials per Mintel surveys.

Second, operational agility: We've rolled out SAP S/4HANA across 80% of facilities, cutting inventory days by 15 to 45 days and improving forecast accuracy to 92%. Commodity hedging covers 85% of 2024 needs—sugar locked at $0.18/lb, dairy at levels 10% below spot—positioning us ahead of peers like General Mills, who cited input cost pressures last quarter.

Third, sustainable growth: ESG is core; our Scope 3 emissions down 18% via regenerative agriculture with 50,000 acres of supplier farms, aligning with EU deforestation regs. This has unlocked $50 million in green financing at 75 basis points below our corporate spread.

Macro headwinds like persistent wage inflation and potential U.S. consumer slowdowns are baked in—we're monitoring DTEI ratios, currently at 28%, down from 32% peaks. But F&B's defensive nature, with 70% of our portfolio in everyday essentials, gives us conviction. Our reaffirmed guide implies modest beats to consensus—Street at $12.75B revenue and $3.28 EPS—but we're focused on execution. Balance sheet remains fortress-like with $2.1B cash, net debt to EBITDA at 2.1x, supporting 50-55 basis points of dividend growth to $1.24/share.

Second, concerning Market share trends for major brands. Before diving deeper, let me set the stage on market share trends for our major brands, which continue to outperform in a dynamic Food & Beverage landscape. We're tracking this through our proprietary analytics dashboard, cross-referenced with syndicated data from NielsenIQ and IRI, focusing on both dollar and unit share across key categories: carbonated soft drinks, ready-to-drink beverages, salty snacks, and better-for-you nutritionals. Overall, in Q3, we expanded our total company market share by 110 basis points year-over-year to 14.7% in North American CPG channels, driven by volume velocity gains of +3.2% and targeted distribution expansions.

Starting with our flagship Apex Cola in the CSD segment. Despite ongoing category headwinds—global CSD volumes down 2.8% YoY per Nielsen—Apex Cola bucked the trend, gaining 1.4 percentage points of dollar share to reach 22.3% in U.S. supermarkets and convenience stores. This marks our 11th straight quarter of share gains versus Coca-Cola, which slipped 80 basis points to 38.2%, and PepsiCo's core brands, down 60 basis points to 24.1%. Key drivers include our Zero Heroes low-calorie reformulation, which captured 15% of new trial in the diet segment, and a 25% uplift in ACV distribution from 92% to 96.4% through hyper-localized merchandising in high-velocity club channels like Costco and Sam's Club. Pricing discipline also played a role—we implemented a modest 4.2% list price increase mid-quarter, maintaining 2.1x category average velocity while preserving household penetration at 68%.

Shifting to RTD beverages, our HydroBoost functional water brand delivered exceptional results, expanding share by 2.7 points to 18.9% in the combined sparkling and enhanced water category, now valued at $12.4 billion annually in the U.S. This outpaced category leader LaCroix, down 1.2 points to 21.5%, and PepsiCo's Bubly, flat at 14.3%, fueled by our electrolyte-infused variants that align with the +11% YoY growth in hydrationals. We've leaned into technical initiatives like our Precision pH Balancing process, ensuring a consistent 7.2-7.4 pH for superior taste stability, which resonated in blind taste tests with a 28% preference score over competitors. Distribution wins added 1,800 new SKUs in mass merchandisers, boosting our e-commerce share to 22% on platforms like Amazon Fresh, where velocity is running 40% above brick-and-mortar averages.

In salty snacks, CrunchMax—our baked potato crisp line—gained 90 basis points to 12.6% share in the $8.2 billion U.S. segment, chipping away at Frito-Lay's dominance, down 70 basis points to 42.8%, amid their supply chain disruptions from corn futures volatility. Our air-fried tech reduced oil content by 45% versus traditional frying, appealing to the clean-label wave, with 62% of new households citing healthier indulgence as the purchase driver per IRI Consumer Insights. We also executed a bold regional play in the Southeast, where we flipped 15% of PepsiCo's linear shelf sets through trade spend optimization, lifting regional share by 3.1 points to 16.2%.

For a regional lens: North America remains our fortress, with aggregate share up 140 basis points to 16.2%, but we're accelerating internationally. In APAC, particularly China and India, our brands grew 4.2 points to 9.8% share in modern trade channels, capitalizing on urbanization and the +7.5% category expansion. Apex Cola overindexed in India via localized mango and guava flavors, gaining 2.8 points against local players like Parle Agro, while HydroBoost entered 1,200 new 7-Eleven doors in Southeast Asia. Europe tells a premiumization story—our nutritionals portfolio, including the newly acquired VitaNutri bar line from a European tuck-in deal, boosted share 1.9 points to 11.4% in the $15B health snacks market. Here, regulatory tailwinds from the EU's Nutri-Score labeling favored our front-of-pack claims, eroding Mondelez's 2.1-point loss to 28.3% in chocolate-adjacent categories. Latin America lagged slightly at +0.8 points due to FX headwinds, but Brazil initiatives like co-branded soccer promotions with our Energize sports drink stabilized share at 13.1% versus Red Bull's 19.4%.

Strategically, these trends underscore our Share Fortress framework: ruthless portfolio pruning—we divested two low-single-digit share legacy brands last year, recycling $450 million into high-growth adjacencies; innovation velocity, with 12 new SKUs launching this quarter, 70% of which are testing above 120% of category norms in IRI scan data; and supply chain resilience via our AI-driven demand forecasting, which mitigated 15% of input cost inflation from cocoa and aluminum spikes. Competitively, we're exploiting gaps—PepsiCo's 1.1-point company-wide share erosion stems from slower zero-sugar transitions, while Coca-Cola's focus on away-from-home recovery post-COVID has left at-home channels vulnerable, where we gained 220 basis points.

Looking forward, we see sustained tailwinds from consumer shifts: 68% of shoppers trading up to functional formats per our proprietary Voice of Consumer panel, and e-commerce now 18% of total sales with 2x share in digital. Risks include private label aggression—gaining 0.9 points industry-wide—and potential tariff escalations impacting APAC imports. But with $1.2 billion in planned 2024 trade investments and a robust M&A pipeline targeting 5-7% ROIC assets, we're positioned to push total share toward 16% by year-end.

Third, in terms of Impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions. As we review our results, I'd like to dive deeply into one of the most pressing headwinds we've navigated this quarter: the impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions. These factors have been persistent challenges across the Food & Beverage sector, echoing the experiences of peers like PepsiCo with their potato and corn derivatives, or Mondelez with cocoa and wheat volatility. For Bellavia Foods, with our portfolio spanning carbonated soft drinks, snack bars, ready-to-eat meals, and plant-based beverages, these pressures directly compressed our gross margins by 210 basis points year-over-year, landing at 41.2% for the quarter—down from 43.3% in Q3 2022.

Commodity inflation remains the elephant in the room, driven by a perfect storm of geopolitical tensions, adverse weather, and structural demand shifts. Overall, our blended cost of goods sold rose 17.8% year-over-year, outpacing our 9.2% top-line growth in constant currency. Sugar costs, critical for our 45% beverage segment including flagship brands like ApexQuench and HydroBoost, surged 24% YoY due to El Niño-induced droughts in Brazil, the world's top exporter. Corn derivatives—used in our snack bars and high-fructose corn syrup for sodas—climbed 18% amid U.S. Midwest floods and sustained ethanol demand. Vegetable oils, essential for frying our CrunchMax chips, jumped 22% from lingering effects of the Ukraine conflict disrupting sunflower oil supplies from the Black Sea region. Aluminum for beverage cans rose 15%, mirroring trends at Coca-Cola and Ball Corporation, while PET resin for plastic bottles increased 12% due to ethylene cracker outages in Asia. Freight and energy costs compounded this, with ocean freight up 28% on Red Sea disruptions and diesel surcharges, and natural gas +35% in Europe impacting our powdered dairy mixes. This inflation accelerated mid-quarter, with a 5-point sequential spike in September tied to Hurricane Idalia's toll on Florida citrus, affecting our juice blends, and labor strikes at U.S. West Coast ports.

Beyond costs, disruptions eroded our supply chain velocity by 14%, as measured by our days inventory outstanding, which expanded to 52 days from 45 last year. Port and logistics congestion, similar to the 2021 Suez Canal crisis, Houthi attacks in the Red Sea rerouted 12% of our Asia-to-Europe shipments via the Cape of Good Hope, adding 18-22 days to lead times and inflating air freight usage by 40% for high-margin items like our protein shakes. In North America, Teamsters negotiations at UPS and port terminals created a 10% shortfall in trucking capacity, delaying 15% of our snack deliveries. Globally, cocoa shortages—up 30% in price—hit our chocolate-coated bars, forcing production halts at two plants. Australian wheat harvests down 11% from La Niña rains disrupted our cereal-based snacks, while palm oil export bans in Indonesia squeezed our bakery lines. These issues translated to $128 million in one-time charges, including $45 million in expedited shipping and $62 million in inventory write-downs for perishable dairy at risk of spoilage.

We've been proactive, clawing back 60% of the inflation through a multi-pronged approach, limiting EPS dilution to $0.18 versus a potential $0.42 without actions. Pricing discipline: implemented targeted price increases averaging 8.5% across 70% of our SKU portfolio, with premiumization in plant-based drinks yielding 92% pass-through. Elasticity remained favorable at -2.1, outperforming category averages per Nielsen data. Hedging and procurement: locked in 65% of 2024 sugar needs at $0.18/lb via futures on ICE, saving an estimated $22 million. Expanded supplier diversification: shifted 25% of corn sourcing from Ukraine/Russia to U.S. and Argentina, and secured long-term contracts with Brazilian sugarcane co-ops. Technical and digital initiatives: rolled out AI-powered predictive analytics via SAP IBP and our proprietary DemandSense platform, improving forecast accuracy to 92%, which reduced stockouts by 22%. Invested $15 million in vertical integration, acquiring a 40% stake in a Midwest corn processing facility. Also piloting blockchain traceability with IBM Food Trust for 30% of cocoa supply to preempt disruptions. Operational efficiencies: our Zero Waste F&B program cut packaging waste 12% through lightweighting cans, saving 8% on aluminum, and dynamic routing software from FourKites optimized truckloads, trimming fuel costs 9%.

Impacts varied by geography, reflecting our 45% North America, 30% EMEA, 20% APAC, and 5% LATAM mix. North America most resilient, with inflation at 14% YoY versus global 18%. Supply chains stabilized post-ports deal, but avian flu drove dairy +20%. EMEA hardest hit at 22% inflation, fueled by energy crises impacting powdered soups and U.K./German plants; offsetting via local sourcing like Turkish wheat. APAC freight disruptions from China port backlogs and Typhoon Doksuri hit juices/snacks; countering with India expansion for spices/pulses. LATAM sugar self-sufficiency buffered us, but coffee volatility pressured RTD coffees.

Looking ahead, we expect input inflation to moderate to 8-10% in FY2024 as El Niño fades and grain harvests normalize, per USDA and Rabobank forecasts. Persistent disruptions like potential U.S. rail strikes or Panama Canal droughts could add 2-3% volatility. We're accelerating our Resilient Supply 2.0 framework: portfolio shift to 25% higher-margin, less commodity-exposed products; sustainability investments of $50 million in regenerative agriculture partnerships with ADM for sustainable soy, securing 20% of oils; M&A focus on bolt-on acquisitions in vertical farms. While these shaved 150bps off full-year gross margins, our actions preserved Adjusted EBITDA margins at 22.1%—above our 20% target and in line with peers like Kellogg or Campbell's.

Fourth, looking at Impact of new product innovations and launches. One of our key growth drivers this quarter was the impact of our new product innovations and launches. We've long prioritized a robust innovation pipeline to capture the accelerating trends in health & wellness, premiumization, and sustainability within the Food & Beverage sector. This quarter, our new product initiatives delivered outsized results, contributing 18% to our overall top-line growth and expanding adjusted EBITDA margins by 220 basis points year-over-year.

Our flagship launch in the plant-based snacking category: VitaBars Pro—a high-protein, clean-label bar fortified with pea protein isolate and upcycled chickpea flour, targeting the $12 billion global plant-based snack market, growing at a 12% CAGR according to Nielsen data. We rolled this out in North America in late Q2, and it ramped to $28 million in Q3 net sales, representing 25% velocity growth versus our legacy protein bars. Distribution expanded to 85% ACV in major chains like Whole Foods and Kroger, with repeat purchase rates hitting 42%—well above the category average of 35%. Margins here are strong at 38% gross, thanks to localized sourcing from U.S. Midwest pea growers, which reduced logistics costs by 15% and aligned with our sustainability commitments under the Science Based Targets initiative.

Complementing this, in the ready-to-drink functional beverage space, HydraGlow Shots—our zero-sugar, electrolyte-infused shots with adaptogens like ashwagandha and electrolytes from coconut water—generated $42 million in incremental revenue. This taps into the $8.5 billion U.S. RTD functional drinks market, where Celsius and Prime have set the pace with 30%+ category growth. Our shots achieved 22% market share in the subcategory within test markets, driven by e-commerce velocity on Amazon up 150% MoM and partnerships with Planet Fitness for in-gym merchandising. These products command a 25% price premium over standard sports drinks, boosting our blended RTD ASP by 11%.

Regionally, North America accounted for 65% of new product sales at $45 million, with robust trial from Gen Z consumers via TikTok Shop integrations, converting 18% of social impressions to baskets. APAC delivered 35% YoY growth in new launches, led by VitaBars Pro localized with matcha and yuzu flavors for Japan and Southeast Asia, adding $12 million through partnerships with 7-Eleven Japan and Alibaba's Freshippo. This reflects our glocal strategy—adapting formulations for regional tastes while leveraging shared R&D platforms. Europe lagged slightly at 10% growth due to stringent clean-label regs under the EU Green Deal, but HydraGlow Shots gained traction in the UK with 15% share in Holland & Barrett stores post-Brexit tariff optimizations.

On the technical side, our $75 million R&D spend—up 20% YoY—fueled these wins through initiatives like AI-driven flavor profiling with Givaudan and high-throughput extrusion tech for bar texturization, cutting development cycles from 18 to 9 months. We've also integrated regenerative agriculture via our partnership with General Mills' 2030 Goals framework, sourcing 40% of ingredients from verified farms, which de-risks supply chains amid climate volatility and enhances our ESG scoring to 85/100 on Sustainalytics.

Strategically, these innovations are accretive across the P&L: new products achieved 45% gross margins versus our company average of 36%, driving 300 basis points of overall margin expansion. They've also fueled portfolio synergies—cross-selling VitaBars with our legacy nut butters lifted category basket size by 22%. Looking ahead, our Q4 pipeline includes three launches: a fiber-enriched RTD coffee rivaling Chobani's Creamers, fermented kombucha sodas akin to Olipop's prebiotic boom, projected $60M run-rate, and upcycled protein crisps. We expect new products to contribute 22-25% of FY24 revenue growth, with APAC scaling to 30% of total innovation sales. Challenges remain—input cost inflation on pea protein up 8% QoQ and competitive intensity from private label at Walmart—but our SKU rationalization culling 15% of underperformers and velocity-based funding model ensure disciplined execution. Innovation is our moat in a $4.5 trillion F&B industry shifting toward functional, sustainable premiumization.

Fifth, reviewing Organic revenue growth: overall and by region. Our organic revenue growth came in at 5.2% year-over-year on a constant currency basis. This marks our sixth consecutive quarter of positive organic growth, outpacing the global F&B industry average of around 3% as reported by NielsenIQ data. Excluding the impacts of acquisitions, divestitures, and foreign exchange—which headwinded reported revenues by 1.8 percentage points—this performance underscores the strength of our core operations amid a still-challenging macroeconomic environment.

Organic growth was driven by a healthy 3.1% price/mix benefit and 2.1% volume growth. Pricing actions were disciplined, averaging mid-single digits globally, reflecting our strategic response to persistent input cost inflation in commodities like cocoa, coffee, and dairy—which remain up 15-20% YoY per the USDA and ICO indices. Volume gains were fueled by mix shift toward higher-margin premium and health-focused SKUs, where we saw double-digit growth. Innovation played a pivotal role here, with launches like our VitaHarvest Plant-Powered Protein Bars—inspired by category leaders like Kind Snacks and RXBAR—contributing over 150 basis points to overall growth through rapid velocity gains in North American club channels.

North America, 42% of total revenue, organic growth was robust at 7.5%, our strongest regional performance and well ahead of peers like General Mills and Kellogg, who reported mid-single-digit gains. Volumes grew 4.2%, propelled by share gains in the snack aisle—up 110 basis points to 14.2% per IRI data—driven by our expanded Harvest Crunch Oven-Baked Veggie Chips line, which benefited from a 25% distribution uplift in mass retailers like Walmart and Kroger. Price/mix added 3.3%, with premium pricing on RTD beverages holding firm despite softer at-home consumption trends. A key technical initiative here was our AI-powered demand sensing platform, rolled out across 80% of our NA supply chain, which improved forecast accuracy by 12% and reduced stockouts by 18%, directly supporting volume momentum.

Europe, Middle East & Africa, EMEA, 28% of revenue, we delivered solid 4.1% organic growth, navigating regulatory headwinds and muted consumer sentiment in Western Europe. Volumes were flat at +0.2%, but mix improvements from healthier options—like our low-sugar EuroFresh Functional Juices, akin to Innocent Smoothies' portfolio—offset declines in legacy sugary beverages, which faced 5-7% volume pressure from UK sugar taxes and EU front-of-pack labeling. Pricing contributed a strong 3.9%, above our guided range, as we passed through 60% of dairy and wheat cost inflation. Strategically, we're accelerating our sustainability playbook: 40% of EMEA SKUs now carry Rainforest Alliance certification, boosting loyalty among Gen Z consumers and driving a 15% premium in e-commerce channels like Ocado and Amazon Fresh. Our new Milan distribution hub, operational since Q1, cut lead times by 22%, enhancing service levels to 97%.

Asia-Pacific, APAC, 18% of revenue, growth accelerated to 6.8% organically, fueled by 4.5% volume expansion in a rebounding out-of-home channel post-COVID restrictions. China and India were standouts: In China, RTD tea and functional waters grew 12%, capturing share from local players like Master Kong through our localized ZenHarvest Infused Waters with adaptogens like ginseng. India saw 9% growth in spices and snacks, leveraging festive season pre-packs similar to Britannia Biscuits' playbook. Price/mix was +2.3%, moderated by competitive intensity, but our e-commerce penetration hit 22% of sales—up from 15% last year—thanks to partnerships with Alibaba and Flipkart. A critical enabler was our precision agriculture tech in Southeast Asia, partnering with Syngenta to stabilize palm oil yields amid El Niño volatility, securing 85% of supply at budgeted costs.

Latin America, LATAM, 12% of revenue, organic growth moderated to 3.2%, impacted by 8% FX headwinds from currency devaluations in Brazil and Argentina. On a constant currency basis, volumes rose 2.8%, led by beer adjacencies and hydration products—our AguaVita Electrolyte Drinks gained 3 share points in Mexico versus Danone's waters. Pricing was +0.4%, as hyperinflation in Argentina capped actions, but we offset this through 10% mix shift to value-added dairy like plant-based yogurts. Looking ahead, we're investing $50M in a new Colombian co-packing facility to localize 70% of beverage production, reducing import tariffs by 15% and improving agility against commodity swings in sugar and corn.

This 5.2% organic growth profile reflects our Premiumize, Localize, Digitize strategy bearing fruit: 60% of incremental revenue from premium/health platforms, 25% from localized assortments, and efficiency gains from $120M in supply chain tech investments YTD. We're confident in delivering full-year organic growth of 4-6%, with upside from Q4 holiday ramps and pipeline innovations like upcycled ingredient snacks.

Sixth, analyzing Organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter/year. As we turn to our outlook, I'm pleased to provide our guidance for organic sales growth, which we define as net revenue growth excluding the impacts of acquisitions, divestitures, and foreign exchange. This metric remains our north star for underlying business performance, stripping out noise to focus on what we control: volume, pricing, mix, and distribution.

In Q3, we delivered organic sales growth of 6.2%, ahead of our initial guide, driven by 3.1% volume gains—our strongest in two years—paired with 2.8% pricing actions and a 0.3% mix benefit from premiumization in our Health & Wellness segment. This builds on the 5.4% organic growth we posted for the first nine months of FY2024, outpacing the industry average of 3.8% per IRI and Nielsen syndicated data for center-store categories.

We're guiding to 5% to 7% organic sales growth for Q4 FY2024, which would mark our fourth consecutive quarter of acceleration. For the full FY2025, we expect organic sales growth of 4% to 6%, positioning us at the high end of our long-term 3% to 5% algorithm amid a still-choppy macro environment. This guidance assumes stable FX rates, moderating but persistent food-at-home inflation around 2-3% as forecasted by the USDA, and cocoa prices stabilizing post their 150% YTD surge—now trading at ~$10,000 per metric ton after peaking near $12,000.

Beverages, 45% of sales, expecting 6-8% organic growth in Q4, led by 4% volume uplift from our re-launched Zero Sugar line, which saw 25% household penetration growth in IRI-tracked channels. Our plant-based VitaGreen functional beverages—infused with adaptogens like ashwagandha—are gaining traction, with distribution up 15% to 12,000 ACV points in North America, mirroring success stories like PepsiCo's Poppi acquisition momentum. Pricing remains disciplined at +2-3%, offsetting input costs from aluminum up 5% QoQ.

Snacks & Confectionery, 35% of sales, 4-6% growth, with volumes flat to +2% as consumers trade down to value packs amid wallet pressures. Innovation is key: our NutriCrunch high-protein bars, now with 15g protein per serving, are driving 12% velocity gains in convenience channels, similar to Mondelez's performance with protein-fortified Oreos. We're also optimizing shelf space, targeting +500 basis points in ACV through planogram resets with Walmart and Kroger.

Health & Wellness Packaged Foods, 20% of sales, highest growth at 7-9%, fueled by 5% volume from organic and keto offerings. Our PureHarvest gluten-free granolas have expanded into 8,000 club stores, echoing Nestlé's Skin Health momentum, with e-commerce sales up 30% YoY via Amazon and Instacart.

North America, 65% of sales, core to our guide at 5-7% growth. Food-away-from-home channels are rebounding to 85% of pre-COVID levels per Black Box Intelligence, boosting our single-serve packs. EMEA, 20% of sales, 6-8% organic, strongest in the portfolio. UK and Germany volumes are up 4% on premium dairy alternatives, with our almond milk line gaining 2 points of market share versus Danone's Alpro. APAC & LatAm, 15% of sales, 3-5% growth, tempered by FX headwinds in Brazil but offset by China expansion. We're rolling out low-sugar ready-to-drink teas into 5,000 Tmall outlets, targeting the $15B RTD tea market growing at 8% CAGR per Euromonitor.

Our confidence stems from three pillars. First, pricing discipline: We've embedded +2-3% structural pricing into contracts, with dynamic pricing tools analyzing 50M+ weekly POS data points to optimize elasticity—yielding a price-to-cost pass-through ratio of 1.1x, better than peers like Kellogg's recent 0.9x. Second, innovation and portfolio health: 40% of FY2025 growth from new products, including AI-driven formulation for our SmartSip electrolyte waters, reducing sugar by 50% while maintaining taste profiles via stevia-peptide blends. Third, supply chain and go-to-market excellence: Post our SAP S/4HANA ERP rollout, inventory turns improved to 8.2x from 6.9x, cutting working capital by 200 bps. Distribution initiatives include +10% e-commerce penetration to 18% of sales, leveraging DoorDash partnerships, and precision farming for cocoa via satellite monitoring—reducing volatility by 15% versus industry benchmarks.

Risks to note: Elevated commodity volatility like sugar at $0.25/lb and potential consumer downtrading if unemployment ticks above 4.2%. But our 55% gross margin trajectory—up from 52% last year—gives us firepower for $300M in targeted marketing behind hero SKUs. This guidance reflects durable momentum from health trends, operational rigor, and category tailwinds in a 2-4% industry backdrop.

Seventh, examining Performance of key brands and product categories. Let me provide some color on the performance of our key brands and product categories, which drove our overall organic sales growth of 6.2% year-over-year, outpacing the global CPG industry average of 3.8% as reported by NielsenIQ. This resilience reflects our disciplined execution amid persistent inflationary headwinds, supply chain normalization, and shifting consumer behaviors toward premiumization and health-focused options. I'll break this down by our four core pillars: Beverages, Snacks & Confectionery, Dairy & Alternatives, and Nutrition & Wellness.

Beverages, 28% of our portfolio, delivered net sales of $1.42 billion, up 8.1% organically. Volume grew 4.2%, fueled by mix shift toward higher-margin RTD formats, while pricing contributed 3.9%. Our flagship HydroBoost brand, our purified and enhanced water line akin to Nestlé's Pure Life, saw double-digit growth of 12.5%, gaining 1.2 share points in the U.S. hydration category to 18.4% per IRI data, driven by our Hydrate Smart campaign emphasizing electrolytes and sustainable packaging. SparkleFizz, our sparkling beverage portfolio competing with PepsiCo's Bubly, surged 15% on the back of low- and no-sugar variants, capturing millennial and Gen Z preferences amid the global soda volume decline of 2.1%. VoltEdge energy drinks grew 9.8%, though we lapped tougher comps from last year's category boom. North America was the star at +10.2% organic growth, bolstered by away-from-home recovery in quick-service restaurants; APAC contributed +7.5% via e-commerce penetration in China, now at 22% of sales versus 14% last year; EMEA lagged at +3.1% due to UK volume pressures from health levies. We're accelerating our $150 million investment in precision fermentation for natural flavors, aiming to reduce sugar content by 20% across the portfolio by FY24.

Snacks & Confectionery, 32% of sales at $1.78 billion, up 5.4% organically—solid given salty snack category inflation outpacing wage growth at 7.2% per Kantar. CrunchMax chips, our hero brand in the $25 billion U.S. savory space rivaling Frito-Lay, posted 7.2% growth with 0.8 share gains to 14.1%, propelled by air-fried and baked variants that resonated with at-home indulgence trends. Volume was flat at +0.1%, but premium mix—think our new truffle-infused line—lifted pricing to +5.3%. BlissBites sweet treats grew modestly at 3.9%, challenged by cocoa costs up 45% YOY, but our plant-based chocolate alternatives mitigated margin erosion to 250 bps expansion. In Latin America, we gained 150 bps in distribution ACV to 92%, powering +11% regional growth amid Brazil's convenience store boom. EMEA faced headwinds from private label aggression, down 1.2% in volume, prompting us to prune 5% of low-velocity SKUs. Our SnackSmart AI platform, leveraging machine learning for demand forecasting, improved inventory turns by 18% and reduced stockouts by 25% QoQ.

Dairy & Alternatives, 22% of the mix at $1.15 billion, surged 9.7% organically, outpacing the 4.5% category growth per Circana. VitaYog, our yogurt powerhouse echoing Chobani's trajectory, exploded 14.3% on Greek and high-protein SKUs, with U.S. market share climbing to 16.7% and refrigerated distribution gains of 400 basis points. GreenMoo plant-based dairy—oat and almond milks competing with Oatly—rocketed 22.1%, riding the 28% global alt-dairy expansion amid lactose intolerance awareness. Pricing held firm at +4.2% despite dairy commodity volatility, with volumes up 5.5%. APAC was exceptional at +13.4%, led by Indonesia's premium yogurt penetration; North America +10.1%; EMEA softened to +2.9% from fluid milk declines post-Ukraine supply disruptions. Margins expanded 180 bps to 22.4% via our backward integration into oat sourcing, cutting costs 12%. Our 2024 innovation pipeline includes 15 NPDs in fermented alt-dairy, targeting the $12 billion addressable market.

Nutrition & Wellness, our fastest grower at 18% of sales and $0.95 billion, up 7.9% organically. This pillar benefits from secular tailwinds like aging populations and post-pandemic immunity focus. ProFuel protein bars and shakes grew 11.2%, gaining share in the $8 billion bar category against Clif and Quest, with e-commerce now 35% of channel mix. ImmuneBoost functional beverages—vitamin-fortified waters—rose 16.4%. North America led at +9.8%; emerging markets in APAC and LATAM combined for +12.5% via affordable sachets. We've invested $80 million in clinical trials for gut-health probiotics, validating claims that drove 30% velocity uplift in test markets.

Our brand health scores remain top-quartile at 78 per YouGov, with 62% of growth from innovation and premiumization. We're optimizing the portfolio by divesting $200 million in underperforming legacy assets to fuel M&A in high-growth adjacencies like functional snacks. This positions us for 5-7% organic growth in FY24, even as input costs stabilize.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Maria to provide more detail on our financial results.
